correctness.rationale: Each of the 16 distinct length-four windows must be hit; each mark hits at most four. Equality partitions their starting positions into disjoint consecutive blocks of four, forcing the marks at 4,8,12,16. Every cyclic class contains one unique occurrence of 0000, so a prefix walk anchored there that appends an unused four-gram until all 16 are visited and checks final closure enumerates the classes exactly once. Running python3 /workspace/reproductions/attractor.py generated 16 classes and all 256 cuts, used the union of the occurrence intervals for each nonempty factor to verify full, not just sharp, attractors, and reproduced every frozen TSV witness and minimum, including the lexicographically first five-position witnesses. It returned 192 four-mark cuts, 64 five-mark cuts, and cycle histogram {8:4,12:8,16:4}. No higher-order claim was tested or needed.

evidence: Proposition 41 supplies general bounds and the surrounding text has one four-mark order-four example; Theorem 29 is a prime-order construction.
The matching Resultary claim also gives one universal five-position full attractor, {3,6,9,12,15} zero-based, for all 256 unfoldings.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general bounds and prime-order theorem do not imply the order-four cut counts; the matching census and its stronger uniform witness do cover the frozen finding.
